publications.title: Structured Flocking for Fixed Wing Multiple Agents
publications.subtitle: IFAC PapersOnLine
publications.description: With developments in miniature UAVs, the problem of flocking has gained significant interest in both academia and industry, with applications in ISR, EW, and communication missions. This paper presents a flocking control scheme for a fleet of fixed-wing UAVs with constrained non-holonomic kinematics. The scheme is based on the flocking algorithms of Olfati-Saber and modified dynamic feedback linearization and demonstrates significant improvements in maneuverability and reliability, which are vital for mission performance. The improvements in efficacy and reliability of the scheme are proved through simulations and a Monte Carlo study. With the proposed scheme, a flock of fixed-wing UAVs can reliably form and traverse any time-parameterized trajectory.

Finally secured the YC sticker! This past weekend, Josh Rodriguez , Jack Cappo , Ming Jin Yong , John Peng , & I competed at Y Combinator ’s RoboHacks and built ID0, the agentic hardware robot. Robots today are limited by one thing: their hands. We keep trying to build a single “perfect” gripper, and it ends up being mediocre at most tasks. So we asked: What if the robot just built the right tool for the job? ID0 scans its environment, understands its task, and generates a modular custom end effector using programmatic CAD. It 3D prints it, picks it up, and switches between tools autonomously. But this goes beyond this demo. If robots can make simple tools, it can evolve to more complex tools with sensors, motors, and magnets. AI can simulate thousands of design options and converge on the optimal design before printing anything. We envision this as the future of robotics, from robots learning software skills to custom building the hardware agents/tools necessary to complete any task. Built in 36 hours. Thanks Innate Iterate NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration Google DeepMind ElevenLabs Axel Peytavin Vignesh Anand & everyone else for all the support! Demo below 👇 ...more ...more

Excited to announce my promotion to Engineering Program Manager - Aircraft Integration (L3) at Archer ! It’s been an incredible 9 months of rapid learning, innovation and growth since starting here, and I am extremely grateful to continue working and contributing alongside the best in the business.

Today, Kid version of me would’ve been ecstatic! In one weekend, I got to meet: Chris Paxton from Agility Robotics Real pioneer redefining the frontier of robotic manipulation and bipedal movement 🦾 Kevin M. from NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration Legendary figure in the field leading the agency’s High End Computing Capability Portfolio 🚀 WALL-E Then OG cinematic inspiration that sparked the dream of robotics for us all! It’s surreal how fast things compound when you’re around the right people, working on the right problems, this is exactly why we're so focused on the mission at Solo Tech ! What stood out most wasn’t just the names it was the high quality of builders pushing Physical AI forward. Real systems. Real demos. Real constraints. Huge kudos to @Alex Peytavin and Vignesh Anand from Innate and Simon Lorenzo and Yoan Di Cosmo from Iterate for bringing together such a high-caliber group at YC RoboHacks! Awesome builders. Excellent demos. The future of physical AI looks bright 🌄 #GetSoloTech

We took home the 𝘐𝘯𝘯𝘢𝘵𝘦 𝘎𝘳𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘗𝘳𝘪𝘻𝘦 and 𝘉𝘦𝘴𝘵 𝘜𝘴𝘦 𝘰𝘧 𝘋𝘢𝘵𝘢 at RoboHacks @ YC this weekend! We built 𝘿𝙞𝙢𝙞𝙢𝙖𝙭, a zero-shot spatial memory layer for a general-purpose robot to understand and navigate a completely new environment. To demonstrate, we used a pharmacy setting and made him tend to customers by reading their prescriptions and picking up medicines for them. The hardware acted up like it always does, but the Innate team was super helpful in getting us past those hurdles. Their product as a whole is really awesome, and they have a great setup for robot control and training. By the end, my brain was almost dead from running on only a couple of hours of sleep. I definitely wouldn't have survived without my teammates Praveen , Jash , Naman , Jaskaran , and Debajit . Thanks to Innate and Iterate for organizing, and Google DeepMind , Scale AI , and Y Combinator for sponsoring this event! Check out our project and demo video here: https://lnkd.in/gckRhXcZ
